question_text: Calculate the radius of a tantalum (Ta) atom, given that Ta has a BCC crystal structure, a density of 16.6 $\mathrm{g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$, and an atomic weight of $180.9 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$.The unit of the answer is nm.
response:
For a BCC metal, the conventional cubic unit cell has $Z=2$ atoms and volume $V=a^3$, with the atoms touching along the body diagonal: $4R = a\sqrt{3}$, so $R = a\sqrt{3}/4$.

Using the density relation $\rho = \dfrac{nA}{V N_A}=\dfrac{2A}{a^3 N_A}$:

$$a = \left(\frac{2A}{\rho N_A}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\frac{2(180.9)}{(16.6)(6.022\times10^{23})}\right)^{1/3}\,\text{cm} = 3.308\times10^{-8}\,\text{cm}=0.3308\,\text{nm}$$

$$R = \frac{a\sqrt{3}}{4} = \frac{(0.3308)(1.732)}{4}\,\text{nm}=0.1432\,\text{nm}$$

Limited to 3 significant figures (set by $\rho=16.6$):

$$\boxed{0.143}$$
